stem: A room contains several wilted plants with brown roots. Irrigation history shows the affected zone was repeatedly waterlogged. What is the best specialist conclusion?
choices: The brown roots prove Pythium infection.
Waterlogging proves there is no pathogen.
Both root-pathogen and abiotic oxygen/root-zone stress hypotheses should remain open until additional evidence discriminates them.
The plants should automatically be treated with a fungicide.
rationale: Root browning and wilt can have infectious and abiotic causes; root-zone history is discriminating context but does not by itself prove or exclude a pathogen.
